purpose: Small, source-pinned semantic/control corpus for superconductivity discovery benchmarking. This is not a complete candidate database or a model training set.
claim_ceiling: Literature-reported experimental observations and computational predictions are recorded separately. No prediction in this file is an experimentally confirmed superconductor.

source_register.title: Developing a complete AI-accelerated workflow for superconductor discovery
source_register.primary_claim_boundary: BEE-NET's 0.87 K MAE is versus DFT-based Allen-Dynes labels, not measured Tc. The end-to-end workflow is the stronger benchmark: >1.3 million candidate structures screened to 741 DFT-confirmed stable conventional superconductors (86% final precision after 866 high-accuracy alpha2F computations), with two candidate compositions synthesized and characterized; only Be2Hf2Nb had a single bulk-like heat-capacity jump, while Be2HfNb2 showed multiphase evidence.
source_register.reported_architecture: Bootstrapped ensemble of equivariant graph convolutional networks; CSO (structure only) and CPD (structure plus coarse phonon DOS) variants; six models across MSE, WMSE and EMD losses
source_register.reported_optimization: 100 bootstrapped ensembles for each CSO and CPD model; 62% unique train data sampled, 38% unique points for validation within training split
source_register.reported_pipeline: 1.22 million generated candidates -> 974k Eg screen -> 822k Ef screen -> 15k BEE-NET Tc > 5 K -> 5.6k M3GNet Eh <= 200 meV/atom -> 1.3k DFT-relaxed structures -> 866 high-accuracy alpha2F calculations -> 741 dynamically/thermodynamically stable compounds with DFT Tc > 5 K; final precision 86%
limitations: BEE-NET is trained on conventional electron-phonon alpha2F data at ambient pressure; do not extrapolate its Tc predictor directly to hydrides or unconventional nickelates.

Pipeline M3GNet formation-hull filter systematically underpredicted Eh by approximately 140 meV/atom in retrospective analysis; this increased recall at expense of precision and its uncorrected effect must remain explicit.
Be2HfNb2 showed two distinct specific-heat jumps and evidence for a multiphase sample; do not classify as unambiguous single-phase bulk superconductivity.
Be2Hf2Nb showed one specific-heat jump with DeltaC/(gamma Tc)=1.44, and the paper reports the sample fully superconducting below approximately 2 K.
Source repository artifact, dataset, model weight and exact split closure remain under audit in issue #12619.

source_register.title: Ambient-pressure 151-K superconductivity in HgBa2Ca2Cu3O8+δ via pressure quench
source_register.thermal_retention: ~149 K retained inside DAC at 77 K for at least 3 days; thermal cycling to room temperature reduced ~147 K to ~143 K; degradation above 200 K reported
source_register.source_status: peer-reviewed publication; not independently reproduced by Symthaea
source_register.primary_claim_boundary: 151 K is an ambient-pressure resistive onset after 10-30 GPa PQP at 4.2 K; it is not a 151 K zero-resistance or thermodynamic transition. Separate retrieved sample showed ~78% magnetic volume fraction at approximately 140 K. State is metastable and thermally/temporally limited. A 172 K observation was not reproduced and remains unresolved.

source_register.title: Complete superconducting phase diagram and flux pinning mechanisms in the yttrium-containing high-entropy alloy YNbTiZrHf
source_register.phase_microstructure: BCC matrix with minor yttrium-rich hexagonal precipitates
source_register.pinning: dominant surface pinning with secondary point contribution; crossover from delta-Tc to delta-l pinning with increasing field
source_register.primary_claim_boundary: Bulk type-II superconductivity confirmed by resistivity, magnetization, AC susceptibility and specific heat. Jc and Hc2 are paper-reported, exact test conditions must be extracted before cross-comparison. The estimated depairing current density is theoretical, not an observed engineering current.

source_register.title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor
source_register.primary_claim_boundary: Science paper reports local shot-noise measurements in Bi2212 at cryogenic STM base temperatures of 4.2 K, 2.3 K and 0.3 K, associating the pseudogap energy with pairing-onset energy and reporting spatially heterogeneous values up to ~70 meV. This is an energy scale, not a transition temperature. Pairing at 300 K is an interpretation/extrapolation, not a direct 300 K measurement. The study does not demonstrate 300 K zero resistance, Meissner response or bulk phase coherence. Local pairing is kept separate from bulk Tc and superfluid stiffness.

source_register.title: Enhancement of superconducting stiffness in hybrid superconducting-metallic bilayers
source_register.primary_claim_boundary: Numerical/theoretical study of Kivelson-style pairing subsystem coupled to a metallic reservoir; pairing and stiffness-limited regimes depend on coupling, filling and density imbalance. Not a physical bilayer experiment or demonstrated increase in an actual material Tc.

source_register.title: Superconducting coherence boosted by outer-layer metallic screening in multilayered cuprates

reported_findings.inner_plane_state: inner CuO2 planes show superconducting signatures while heavily overdoped outer planes remain metallic at low temperature
reported_findings.proximity: no detectable superconducting proximity signal in outer planes
reported_findings.screening_mechanism: metallic outer planes screen dopant-layer disorder from the inner superconducting plane; model calculations indicate weak interlayer wavefunction mixing
screening_metrics_proposed: ARPES quasiparticle peak width / scattering rate

source_register.primary_claim_boundary: This is a combination of ARPES observations and model calculations, not a demonstrated increase in the transition temperature of the surface-doped crystal. The >95% outer-plane wavefunction confinement is calculated. The paper does not report a newly determined Tc for the surface-doped state; do not substitute bulk baseline Tc values from a different specimen or composition. It is a screening/disorder-control mechanism distinct from direct pair transfer into a metallic reservoir.

source_register.title: Superconducting 2D cuprate with a single CuO2 plane

reported_findings.optimal_transition_effect: approximately 10% reduction in optimal Tc relative to thicker/bulk Bi-2201
reported_findings.anomalous_metal: anomalous metallic state observed between insulating and superconducting regimes as temperature approaches zero

source_register.data_availability: datasets available from corresponding authors upon request
source_register.primary_claim_boundary: This is a dimensionality and quantum phase-transition reference, not a higher-Tc discovery. The ~10% reduction is a reported dimensionality effect. The data are available on request; no local raw data were mirrored.

source_register.title: The emergence of global phase coherence from local pairing in underdoped cuprates
source_register.method: scanning tunnelling microscopy and quasiparticle interference

reported_findings.phase_ordering_mechanism: global phase coherence appears when spatial occupation of a checkerboard plaquette charge-order pattern exceeds a threshold
reported_findings.local_spectra: local spectra remain qualitatively similar across the insulator-to-superconductor boundary

source_register.primary_claim_boundary: This is an experimental local-to-global coherence result in underdoped Bi-La-Sr-Cu-O. The reported threshold is for the studied material and charge-order texture; it is not a universal occupancy constant or a general design recipe.

source_register.title: Phase transition in the cuprates from a magnetic-field-free stiffness meter viewpoint
source_register.method: field-free superconducting-ring magnetic moment measurement, complemented by low-energy muSR

reported_findings.comparison: in-plane current path versus interplane current path
reported_findings.result: different transition temperatures for the two current geometries, identifying a range with two-dimensional stiffness
reported_findings.validation: low-energy muSR measured stiffness anisotropy below Tc

source_register.primary_claim_boundary: A measurement-method reference for extracting anisotropic stiffness; not a new material or room-temperature superconductivity result.

source_register.title: Measuring kinetic inductance and superfluid stiffness of two-dimensional superconductors using high-quality transmission-line resonators
source_register.method: high-Q superconducting transmission-line resonators; kinetic-inductance and loss measurement

reported_findings.kinetic_inductance_precision: up to approximately one part per million
reported_findings.validation: aluminium results compared with BCS theory; demonstrated on multilayer NbSe2

source_register.primary_claim_boundary: Kinetic inductance is a useful stiffness metrology observable, but conversion to penetration depth or superfluid stiffness depends on sample geometry, current profile, locality, anisotropy and nonlocal electrodynamics. The paper explicitly discusses these limits; do not use a universal geometry-free conversion.
